extracted.intended_audience: corporate accountants, corporate finance teams, SEC filing preparers, and securities lawyers advising on business combination reporting
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on performing SEC Regulation S‑X/Rule 11‑01 significance tests for acquired businesses, including aggregation, timing, financial statement periods and required adjustments when preparing Form 8‑K, amended filings and registration statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation of individually insignificant acquisitions — period
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual acquisitions that are aggregated include those that occur or are probable‑to‑occur from the balance sheet date of the most recently filed audited annual financial statements through the effective date of the registration statement or mailing date of certain proxy materials. Any acquisitions predating the most recently filed audited balance sheet date are disregarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing of a Form 10‑K establishes a new balance sheet date for determining which prior acquisitions to aggregate. Obtaining and filing audited interim period financial statements does not create a fresh start date. Because filing a Form 10‑K creates a new balance sheet date, the aggregation period from the prior balance sheet date through effectiveness may exceed 12 months (e.g., registration declared effective shortly after fiscal year end but before Form 10‑K is filed). [FRM 2035.4]

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation requirement for Form 8‑K (related vs unrelated)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form 8‑K only requires aggregating individually insignificant acquisitions if they are related businesses and, in aggregate, are more than 20% significant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because unrelated acquired businesses are not related, Form 8‑K is not required regardless of the group's level of significance. See Form 8‑K Item 2.01 (Instruction 4) and related Q&As (e.g., Questions 2.2.230 and section 3.3.30).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reperformance of significance tests after reissued (retrospectively adjusted) financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant must perform the S‑X Rule 3‑05 significance tests based on its newly filed revised financial statements in connection with a registration or proxy statement if the revised financial statements have been retrospectively adjusted for discontinued operations (Subtopic 205‑20), a change in accounting principle (Topic 250), or a reorganization of entities under common control to which as‑if pooling is applied (Subtopic 805‑50).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To comply in a new registration or proxy statement, the registrant must perform significance tests based on the newly filed revised financial statements that reflect the retrospective adjustment for: (a) individual businesses acquired after the date the retrospectively adjusted financial statements are filed; (b) probable acquisitions; and (c) aggregate impact of all individually insignificant businesses that have occurred since the end of the most recently completed fiscal year. For individual businesses acquired on or before the date the revised statements are filed, the registrant may determine significance using either the audited annual financial statements on file before the registrant files revised audited annual financial statements or the revised audited annual financial statements, but must be consistent in the choice for all such acquisitions in that registration statement. This choice can affect whether previously filed Form 8‑K financial statements must be updated. [FRM 2025.1]

rubrics_metrics.name: Option to rely on original significance determination vs reperformance
rubrics_metrics.description: When financial statements are revised after an acquisition, a registrant may either continue to rely on the significance tests performed at the acquisition date or reperform the tests using the revised financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuing to rely on the original determination may require updating financial statements previously filed on Form 8‑K/A (and updating pro forma information) to meet age and presentation requirements. Reperforming the tests using revised reported amounts may change the significance outcome and can avoid the need to update previously filed statements or pro forma information if the revised outcome is below significance thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial statement period to use for significance tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance tests are performed using the registrant’s last annual audited financial statements that were required to be filed with the SEC before the tested business acquisition was consummated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ordinarily those are the audited financial statements included in the most recently filed Form 10‑K. If an acquisition is consummated shortly after the registrant’s fiscal year‑end (and the most recent year‑end statements are not yet required to be filed), the registrant may choose to use the prior fiscal‑year financial statements. See S‑X Rule 11‑01(b)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using interim periods for significance tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants are prohibited from using audited or unaudited interim period balances to perform the tests of significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prohibition applies even if there has been a significant change in size or circumstances during subsequent interim periods (e.g., completing an offering that materially increases total assets). A registrant that believes interim results make the outcome unrepresentative may request a waiver from the SEC staff. [FRM 2020.1]

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of financial information not yet required to be filed (shortly after year‑end flexibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an acquisition is consummated shortly after the registrant’s fiscal year‑end and the fiscal year‑end financial statements are not yet required to be filed, the registrant may determine significance based on either its most recently completed fiscal year or the prior fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The choice can benefit registrants that experienced significant increases in denominators used in the tests (e.g., total assets, revenues, net income). This flexibility may not be available for initial public offerings; see section 7.2.30 for IPO considerations. [S‑X Rule 11‑01(b)(3)(i)(C), Regs Comm 03/2021]

rubrics_metrics.name: Using acquired business unaudited financial statements for tests
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant can use the acquired business’s unaudited financial statements to perform the significance tests, provided those unaudited statements reflect necessary adjustments to comply with accounting standards and Regulation S‑X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the acquired business is ultimately significant, audited financial statements must be filed. If audited statements differ from the unaudited amounts used initially, the registrant must reperform the significance tests based on the audited statements to determine actual significance, which then determines which periods are required to be presented. Differences that alter required financial statement periods can increase effort to meet the 71‑day amended Form 8‑K deadline and may affect eligibility to use Form S‑3 if required statements are not timely filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to perform tests when no prior stand‑alone financial statements exist
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant must perform the significance tests even if there are no previous stand‑alone financial statements for the acquired business (e.g., acquisitions of a division or product line).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If available, carve‑out financial statements may be used in lieu of full financial statements; carve‑outs must reflect the acquired component’s operating history as if it had operated on a stand‑alone basis and include allocations of certain indirect costs. When full or carve‑out statements are impracticable, abbreviated financial statements may be used in certain circumstances (see section 10.3.20 and 10.3.30 for additional guidance). [S‑X Rule 11‑01(b)(3)(i)(A)]

rubrics_metrics.name: Different fiscal year‑ends between registrant and acquired business
rubrics_metrics.description: Fiscal year‑ends need not be consistent. The registrant uses: (a) its fiscal year‑end financial statements that were required to be filed for the period before the acquisition; and (b) the acquired business’s most recent fiscal year‑end financial statements that would have been required if that business had the same filer status as the registrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fiscal periods are not conformed for purposes of the tests — do not add partial periods from different fiscal years or annualize a portion of results. Special guidance exists for situations that may involve using fewer than 12 months of operating results under the income test (see Question 3.5.170). Examples illustrate use of different year‑ends (e.g., registrant June 30 vs acquired company March 31). [S‑X Rule 11‑01(b)(3)(i)]

rubrics_metrics.name: Change in periods used for individual vs aggregate significance tests
rubrics_metrics.description: The financial statement periods used to determine aggregate significance may differ from those used to determine individual significance at the acquisition date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For an individual acquisition (e.g., Form 8‑K requirement), use the registrant’s most recent fiscal year required to be filed as of the date of the individual acquisition. For an aggregate significance test performed later (e.g., in connection with a registration statement), use the registrant’s most recent fiscal year‑end required to be filed as of the effective date of the registration statement. The same concept applies when aggregating related businesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amounts must be determined under the same accounting standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The financial information (total assets, revenue, net income, etc.) for both the acquired business and the registrant used to determine significance must be determined using the same comprehensive basis of accounting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A registrant that files US GAAP financial statements (or must reconcile to US GAAP) performs the significance tests using US GAAP (as applicable to PBEs) amounts for the acquired business. A registrant that files under IFRS uses amounts determined under IFRS. [S‑X Rule 1‑02(w)(1), FRM 2015.3]

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustments for private company accounting alternatives (generally prohibited)
rubrics_metrics.description: The financial information of the acquired business used to perform significance tests may not be prepared using private company accounting alternatives; amounts must be adjusted to exclude the effects of those alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, if the acquired business had elected to amortize goodwill in pre‑acquisition statements, the registrant must exclude the effects of goodwill amortization and determine whether to include any impairment charges based on retrospective goodwill impairment tests. Exception: the SEC staff permits a registrant to determine significance using an acquired business’s financial information that includes the effects of applying the 'risk‑free rate' private company alternative in Topic 842 (lease rate). [Regs Comm 03/2014; Regs Comm 10/2020]
